Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure is due to a NullPointerException (NPE) when StringUtils.join is called with an array containing an object whose toString method returns null. The current bug report reproduces this with an anonymous class overriding toString() to return null, which is a rare but valid scenario.

Inspecting the method StringUtils.join(Object[], String, int, int) shows that inside the join method, it initializes a StringBuilder based on the length of array[startIndex].toString(). However, this call assumes that toString() returns a non-null String but does not guard against a null return value. This can cause a NullPointerException at line 3383 during the construction of the StringBuilder.

Further, in the loop appending each array element (lines 3385-3392), it appends the element itself, which implicitly calls toString(), but it does not handle when toString returns null—it only checks if the element is null.

Therefore, when any element's toString returns null, the StringBuilder initialization and the append call can throw an NPE. The existing code does not handle or defend against the case where toString returns null, assuming it never happens. This matches the reported failure and the test, which fails because an element's toString returns null.

Consequently, the root cause is that the join method does not handle or guard against toString returning null on any element in the array.

Recent bug reports are unrelated and do not impact this diagnosis.

The fix should be applied to org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.join(Object[], String, int, int) method to handle null returned from toString safely (for example, replacing null with "null" string).
